> think that the problem with it was people not being skilful enough to
> work around it, or was it "too" powerful?"

If so, the question is either insincere or ridiculous. Why would one
care so much about LSJ's opinion on Legacy of Pander, and not anyone else's,
unless one wanted to somehow relate that to LSJ's influence on the decision
that resulted in a change to Legacy of Pander?
Not to hack on LSJ here, but if you wanted a player's opinion, why not
ask The Lasombra or Derek Ray? Well, because they're *not* the NetRep.
Honestly, L. Scott has a hard enough job in which he can't please
everyone, and does a damn fine job, all things considered. Considering that
this also isn't a full-time job for him, people shouldn't expect to get to
debate him on every single change made to the game, except on "legal
grounds" (such as rulings that appear inconsistent).
We live under a benevolent dictatorship, and for the good of the game,
shouldn't be changed to democracy, which, in essence, is what getting LSJ to
voice his "personal" opinion is all about.

--
Pat Ricochet
Soul Jar'rn Fool of Atlanta
